title: Prompting Claude to find your approximate search breaking points
text: Nearest few cells. And this is the part that matters, report recall against the exact answer. So we measure what the shortcut costs instead of assuming it is free. Two functions carry the whole idea. Build groups every vector into a cell about the square root of the collection so each cell holds about the square root, too. Search ranks the centroids, takes the nearest few cells, and scans only what is inside them. Everything else is never examined. That is the entire trick. Here's what that buys, 100 times the data. Compare against a third of 1% of the collection and you get a third of the true neighbors back. 1 and 1/3% gets you 60%. 5% gets you 88, 10% gets you 96. Approximate does not mean unpredictable. It means there is a dial and you decide where to set it. So, exact search is correct and does not scale because every comparison still has to happen.
